pedal: A pedal the user chose, unknown to the analysis — blind test (mono: the pedal's input -> its mono output)
comment: The user picks a pedal and its settings and tells nothing: the pedal and its settings are to be read from the recordings. The signals are general ones, each for a family of effects: a sweep (frequency response, a tone's or an EQ's curve; a delay or a reverb smears it), clicks (echoes and their spacing, a reverb's tail, latency), a steady 440 Hz tone (tremolo, chorus, flanger, phaser, rotary: the rate and depth of whatever moves; an octave or pitch effect; distortion's harmonics), five steady tones together (a filter or notches moving over time), a noise staircase and a 1 kHz staircase (what level does: compressor, gate, envelope filter, clipping), plucks (attack and decay behaviour), and two guitar excerpts. The same pedal and settings for every take after the first.

takes.name: bypass-sweep
takes.note: The pedal off (its LED off): the reference. Interface out 3 into the pedal's input (the mono one if it has two), its mono output into front input 2. If it has a second output, leave it empty.
